intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently for an authentic culinary adventure.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Street Food
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, famous for its colorful silk lanterns, French colonial architecture, and vibrant street food scene. Try Cao Lau, White Rose Dumplings, and Banh Mi Phuong. On the 14th of each lunar month, the town turns off electric lights and glows with hundreds of lanterns.

experiences.name: Motorbike Backpacking on the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike and ride the legendary Hai Van Pass between Da Nang and Hue, one of Southeast Asia's most scenic coastal mountain roads. The route offers breathtaking views of the South China Sea, lush jungle, and old French and American war bunkers at the summit. A quintessential backpacker experience in Vietnam.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat Tour & Local Village Visit
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, navigating narrow canals by wooden sampan boat. Visit floating markets, coconut candy workshops, and local villages. Sample tropical fruits, fresh spring rolls, and honey tea while experiencing the rural heartbeat of southern Vietnamese culture.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the electric backpacker hub of Ho Chi Minh City's Bui Vien Street, known as the city's unofficial backpacker district. Enjoy cheap local beers, Vietnamese bar snacks like grilled skewers and fresh spring rolls, live music, and a buzzing multicultural atmosphere. A must-do social experience for budget travelers.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.date: Day 1 - April 15, 2027 (Arrival Day)
day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the 86 airport bus (~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Boutique Stay in Old Quarter, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk around Hoan Kiem Lake (15-min walk from most Old Quarter hostels). Stroll the 36 ancient streets, soak in the atmosphere, and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri-Sun) or wander the lit-up Old Quarter streets. Head to Ta Hien Street ('Beer Corner') for a cheap bia hoi (fresh draught beer, ~5,000-10,000 VND per glass) and meet fellow backpackers.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a bowl of Bun Bo Nam Bo (beef noodle salad) from a street stall near the Old Quarter for ~50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Bun Cha at Bun Cha Huong Lien (famous spot, ~60,000 VND) or a street stall version for ~40,000 VND near Hang Manh Street

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to VND at the airport or an Old Quarter exchange booth (avoid hotel rates). Get a local SIM card at the airport (Viettel or Vietnamobile, ~150,000 VND with data). Budget tip: airport bus is far cheaper than taxis (~400,000 VND) or ride-hail apps.

day_by_day.date: Day 2 - April 16, 2027 (Hanoi Exploration)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a Pho breakfast at a local street stall (~40,000 VND). Walk to Hoan Kiem Lake for the morning tai chi session (free, starts around 6:00-7:30am). Visit Ngoc Son Temple on the lake (entrance ~30,000 VND). Explore the atmospheric streets of the 36 Old Quarter guilds on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first university (~30,000 VND entrance). Walk or take a Grab bike (~20,000-30,000 VND) to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex area — visit the surrounding gardens and the One Pillar Pagoda for free (mausoleum itself is free but check opening hours). Browse the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology if time allows (~40,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Banh Mi Phuong stall or any local banh mi cart (~25,000-35,000 VND). Attend a Bia Hoi corner session on Ta Hien Street. Try Egg Coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at Cafe Giang (~25,000 VND) — a Hanoi specialty.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef pho) from a street stall near the hotel, ~40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Dau Mam Tom (fried tofu with fermented shrimp paste) from a local stall near Temple of Literature, ~40,000-50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from Banh Cuon Ba Hanh on Ngo Si Lien Street, ~50,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — most Old Quarter sights are walkable. Bargain politely at souvenir shops. Avoid tuk-tuk and cyclo tours near the lake as they are tourist traps — walk or use Grab app instead.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Hidden Gems + Day Trip Prep)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dong Xuan Market (Hanoi's largest covered market, free entry) for a chaotic, authentic local shopping experience. Sample street snacks inside. Walk to the Long Bien Bridge for photos and a view of the Red River. Explore the French Quarter on foot — admire colonial architecture around Hoan Kiem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Women's Museum (~30,000 VND) or the Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton', ~30,000 VND) for powerful historical insights. Spend the late afternoon at a local cafe — try Cong Caphe (coconut coffee, ~45,000 VND) for a trendy but affordable break.
day_by_day.evening: Book your onward transport: overnight sleeper bus to Hue or a train ticket to Da Nang for Day 5 (book at a travel agent on Hang Be Street, ~200,000-350,000 VND). Enjoy a final Hanoi street food crawl: try Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish, ~120,000 VND) or cheaper versions at nearby stalls.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street vendor near Dong Xuan Market, ~25,000-30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Pho Cuon (fresh spring rolls) from a stall on Ngu Xa Street near West Lake, ~40,000-50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Mi Quang or Banh Xeo (sizzling crepe) from a local restaurant in the Old Quarter, ~50,000-70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book transport for Day 5 today to secure budget seats. Consider a free walking tour (tip-based) offered by Hanoi Free Tour guides — check Facebook groups. April weather in Hanoi can be warm and humid with occasional drizzle — carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Ninh Binh Day Trip)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~80,000-100,000 VND). Rent a bicycle upon arrival (~50,000-70,000 VND/day) and cycle to Tam Coc. Take a sampan boat ride through the stunning limestone karst caves (~150,000 VND/person, negotiate).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free) carved into the cliffside. Hike up to the viewpoint for panoramic rice paddy and karst views. Visit the ancient capital of Hoa Lu (~20,000 VND entrance) to see the Dinh and Le dynasty temples.
day_by_day.evening: Return by bus to Hanoi (~100,000 VND). Rest at the hostel. Pack your bag for the overnight journey to Hue the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Quick banh mi from a street cart near the bus station before departure, ~25,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or a set lunch at a local Ninh Binh restaurant near Tam Coc, ~60,000-80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Back in Hanoi — Chao (rice porridge) or Bun Rieu (crab noodle soup) from a night stall in the Old Quarter, ~40,000-50,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Start very early (6:30-7:00am) to beat the crowds at Tam Coc. Bring cash — ATMs are limited in Ninh Binh. Wear sunscreen and a hat. Ninh Binh is one of Vietnam's most beautiful and budget-friendly day trips — highly recommended.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 - April 19, 2027 (Travel Day: Hanoi to Hue)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Hanoi hostel. Take an overnight sleeper bus or morning train to Hue (train: ~250,000-350,000 VND soft seat, ~14 hours; or budget flight ~500,000-800,000 VND if booked in advance). If taking the train, enjoy the scenic coastal route through the Hai Van Pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hue (if flying, arrive by afternoon; if bussing/training, enjoy the journey scenery). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Hue's backpacker area (~150,000-200,000 VND/night). Walk along the Perfume River embankment.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hue's Dong Ba Market for local crafts and street food. Stroll along Le Loi Street for cheap eats and local vibe.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Hanoi hostel or grab a quick banh mi before departure, ~25,000 VND
meals.lunch: Snacks and instant noodles on the train/bus (~20,000-30,000 VND) or pack your own from a convenience store
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue beef noodle soup) from a local stall in Hue — the city's signature dish, ~40,000-55,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The train journey from Hanoi to Hue is considered one of the most scenic in Southeast Asia — grab a window seat. Book seats in advance during April (shoulder season). Budget airlines like VietJet or Bamboo Airways often have flash sales for this route.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 - April 20, 2027 (Hue Imperial City)
day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Dai Noi) — the UNESCO-listed walled city (~200,000 VND entrance). Explore the Forbidden Purple City ruins, the Thai Hoa Palace, and the ornate gates. Hire an audio guide for deeper context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000-70,000 VND/day) and ride south along the Perfume River to visit the elaborate royal tombs. Visit Tu Duc Tomb (~150,000 VND) — the most scenic and romantic of the tombs. Optional: visit Minh Mang Tomb for a different architectural style.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town. Walk across Truong Tien Bridge at sunset for river views. Head to Pham Ngu Lao Street for cheap backpacker food and cold beers. Try Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes) and Banh Khoai (Hue sizzling crepe) from a local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Com Hen (baby clam rice) — a Hue breakfast specialty from a local stall near Dong Ba Market, ~30,000-40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Banh Mi Hue or a set lunch near the Citadel, ~30,000-50,000 VND
meals.dinner: A mix of Hue royal cuisine small dishes (Banh Beo, Banh Nam, Banh Loc) at a local restaurant, ~80,000-120,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Hue's royal tombs are spread out — a bicycle is the best budget way to visit multiple. Combine tickets can save money. Hue is famous for its refined, complex cuisine — don't miss the small rice cake dishes unique to this city.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21, 2027 (Hue to Hoi An via Hai Van Pass)
day_by_day.morning: Hire a motorbike taxi (xe om) or join a budget group tour (~200,000-250,000 VND) to ride over the legendary Hai Van Pass to Da Nang. Stop at the top of the pass for breathtaking coastal views. Visit Lang Co Beach briefly for a photo stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Da Nang. Take a local bus or Grab to Hoi An (~30 km south, ~30,000-50,000 VND by bus or ~100,000 VND Grab). Check in to a budget hostel in Hoi An Ancient Town (~150,000-180,000 VND/night). Walk into the UNESCO Ancient Town (free to enter streets, combined ticket for sites ~120,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ancient Town at dusk when lanterns are lit — magical atmosphere. Walk across the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge. Browse the night market at An Hoi Islet. Watch lanterns float on the Thu Bon River.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the Hue guesthouse or a street stall before departure, ~30,000-40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or Banh Mi at a Da Nang street stall during transit, ~40,000-60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) from a local restaurant in the Ancient Town, ~55,000-70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass ride is one of Vietnam's most iconic experiences — made famous by Top Gear. Go early morning for the best light and fewer clouds. If you prefer comfort, the train through the tunnel is an option (~50,000 VND). Hoi An is more expensive than Hanoi or Hue — budget carefully.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 - April 22, 2027 (Hoi An Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and visit the Hoi An Central Market for a vibrant morning atmosphere and cheap local breakfast. Take a cooking class (budget options from ~300,000-400,000 VND including market tour) to learn to make White Rose Dumplings and Cao Lau. Alternatively, explore the Ancient Town's merchant houses (Tan Ky Old House, ~80,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) and ride 4 km to An Bang Beach for a relaxing afternoon swim. Alternatively, visit the My Son Sanctuary (Cham ruins, ~150,000 VND entrance, ~40 km away — join a budget group tour ~200,000-250,000 VND). Return to town for a late afternoon wander through the tailors' street on Le Loi.
day_by_day.evening: Join the lantern-lit Ancient Town evening. Buy a floating lantern (~20,000-30,000 VND) and release it on the Thu Bon River. Enjoy street food at the Hoi An Night Market — try Banh Mi Phuong (arguably Vietnam's best banh mi, ~35,000-45,000 VND).

meals.breakfast: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Vac) from a market stall, ~30,000-40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Ga Hoi An (Hoi An chicken rice) from a local stall — another town specialty, ~50,000-60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Phuong + fresh spring rolls from the night market, ~60,000-80,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Ancient Town is best explored on foot or bicycle. Avoid motorbikes inside the old town (restricted hours). The town is very photogenic at night — bring your camera. Tailoring is a Hoi An specialty — custom clothes can be made in 24-48 hours at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (Travel: Hoi An to Ho Chi Minh City)
day_by_day.morning: Check out of Hoi An hostel. Take a Grab or local bus back to Da Nang Airport (~45 min). Catch a budget flight to Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC/Saigon) — book in advance for ~400,000-700,000 VND with VietJet or Bamboo Airways. Alternatively, take an overnight bus (~200,000-250,000 VND, ~18 hours — depart previous evening).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City. Take a bus from Tan Son Nhat Airport to District 1 (Bus 152, ~6,000 VND — extremely cheap!) or Grab (~100,000-130,000 VND). Check in to a budget hostel in the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district (~150,000-200,000 VND/night). Drop bags and head out to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Ben Thanh Market area for your first taste of Saigon's energy. Explore the chaotic but thrilling street food scene on Pham Ngu Lao and Bui Vien Streets (the famous backpacker street). Watch the nightly street party atmosphere on Bui Vien Walking Street.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick banh mi or xoi from a cart near the Hoi An hostel before checkout, ~25,000-30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Airport food or convenience store snacks during transit, ~50,000-80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Hu Tieu Nam Vang (Phnom Penh-style noodle soup) or Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) from a Saigon street stall, ~50,000-70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Bus 152 from Da Nang Airport is one of Vietnam's great budget travel hacks — 6,000 VND vs 100,000+ VND for a Grab. Book your flight well in advance for the best fares. HCMC is faster-paced and hotter than Hanoi — stay hydrated.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 - April 24, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City Highlights)
day_by_day.morning: Start with a strong Vietnamese iced coffee (Ca Phe Sua Da, ~20,000-30,000 VND) from a sidewalk plastic-stool cafe. Visit the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace, ~40,000 VND) — explore the war-era bunkers and government rooms. Walk to the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) for a sobering but essential perspective on the Vietnam War.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon and the Central Post Office (free, beautiful French colonial architecture). Explore the Ben Thanh Market area — browse but be aware of tourist pricing. Take a Grab to District 3 or District 4 for a more local feel and cheaper street food. Visit Binh Tay Market in Cholon (Chinatown) for an authentic wholesale market experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final Vietnam street food feast on Bui Vien or at a local Com Tam spot. Enjoy a rooftop bar with city views (Saigon Saigon Rooftop Bar or a cheaper local alternative). Reflect on 10 incredible days in Vietnam over a final bia hoi. Pack for departure or onward journey.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (Vietnamese egg banh mi) from a street cart, ~25,000-35,000 VND
meals.lunch: Com Tam Suon Bi Cha (broken rice with grilled pork ribs, shredded pork, and egg cake) — Saigon's iconic dish, ~55,000-75,000 VND
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hotpot) shared with hostel friends at a local budget restaurant, ~100,000-150,000 VND per person, or a final street food crawl sampling Goi Cuon, Banh Trang Tron, and Bo Bia, ~80,000-100,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: HCMC is a great city for a final splurge on a slightly nicer meal — still very affordable by Western standards. Consider a day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~120,000 VND entrance + ~150,000 VND transport) if you have extra time before your flight. Keep some VND for airport transport. Total estimated 10-day budget: 3,000,000-4,500,000 VND (~$120-$180 USD) excluding flights and accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in the Old Quarter (~45 min by taxi or airport bus). Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a walk around the immediate neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore the narrow lanes, browse local craft shops, and soak in the buzzing atmosphere. Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the Ngoc Son Temple on Turtle Island (small entrance fee ~30,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ta Hien Street — known as 'Beer Street' — for a classic Hanoi bia hoi (fresh draft beer, ~10,000 VND/glass) experience. Watch the city come alive at night and enjoy the street-side energy.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) from a street stall near the Old Quarter for ~50,000 VND
meals.dinner: Bun Cha Huong Lien (made famous by Anthony Bourdain) — grilled pork with rice noodles for ~80,000–120,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Keep the first afternoon light due to travel fatigue. Exchange some cash to VND at the airport or a local bank. Grab a local SIM card at the airport for easy navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (check opening hours — closed Mon & Fri afternoons). Explore the Presidential Palace grounds, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entrance) — one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums, showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Spend 2–3 hours exploring indoor and outdoor exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for a self-guided street food crawl. Try Banh Mi from a cart, Pho from a local shop, and finish with Egg Coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at Cafe Giang — a Hanoi institution.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef noodle soup) from a sidewalk stall near the hotel — ~50,000–70,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Thang (delicate Hanoi-style noodle soup) near the museum area — ~60,000 VND
meals.dinner: Street food crawl in the Old Quarter — budget ~100,000–150,000 VND total for multiple small dishes

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum requires modest dress (no shorts or sleeveless tops). Book a taxi or grab bike to the Museum of Ethnology (~20 min from Old Quarter).

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning train or bus to Ninh Binh (~2 hours from Hanoi). Rent a bicycle upon arrival and cycle through the stunning Tam Coc valley — paddy fields, limestone karsts, and river caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Boat trip through Tam Coc caves (~150,000 VND, ~2 hours). Afterward, climb up to Hang Mua viewpoint for a panoramic view over the valley (~100,000 VND entrance). The 500-step climb is rewarding.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus or train. Relax with a light dinner in the Old Quarter. Optional: join the Friday/Saturday night street market if applicable.

meals.breakfast: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a local spot near the hotel before departure — ~40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tam Coc — try Com Rang (fried rice) or grilled goat (de nui), a Ninh Binh specialty — ~80,000–120,000 VND
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric grilled fish with dill and noodles) back in Hanoi — ~120,000–150,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Start early to make the most of Ninh Binh. Bring sunscreen and water — the Hang Mua climb can be hot. Ninh Binh is a great day trip but can also be an overnight if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hanoi for Ha Long Bay — join a 2-day/1-night budget-to-mid-range cruise (~$80–$130 USD per person). Board the junk boat and cruise through the iconic emerald waters and limestone islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through hidden lagoons and sea caves (included in most cruise packages). Swim at a secluded beach on one of the islands. Enjoy the dramatic scenery of Ha Long Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset on the deck with drinks. Communal dinner on the boat featuring fresh seafood — squid, prawns, and fish. Squid fishing off the boat deck at night — a fun social activity with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the bus/van to Ha Long Bay — or grab Xoi (sticky rice) before departure ~30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Included on the cruise boat — fresh Vietnamese seafood spread
meals.dinner: Included on the cruise boat — multi-course seafood dinner

day_by_day.notes: Book the cruise at least 2–3 days in advance. Choose a reputable mid-range operator (e.g., Indochina Junk, Bhaya, or Paradise Cruises economy tier). Pack a small overnight bag — leave large luggage at the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the boat deck. Visit a floating fishing village by kayak or rowboat. Enjoy a final breakfast on board before the cruise returns to port.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hanoi by bus (~3.5 hours). Check back into the hotel, collect luggage, and head to the train station or airport for an overnight train or flight to Hue or Da Nang.
day_by_day.evening: Board the Reunification Express overnight train to Hue (~13 hours, soft sleeper berth ~$25–$35 USD) — a classic backpacker experience with stunning coastal scenery at dawn.

meals.breakfast: Included on the cruise — Vietnamese breakfast spread
meals.lunch: Quick stop at a roadside restaurant en route back to Hanoi — Pho or Com Binh Dan (local rice set meal) ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Mi and snacks from a convenience store or street stall to eat on the overnight train — ~50,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance via Vietnam Railways website or Baolau.com. Soft sleeper (4-berth cabin) is recommended for comfort and safety. Store valuables securely on the train.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Hue in the early morning. Check into a budget-friendly guesthouse in the city center (~$15–$25/night). Freshen up, then head to the Imperial Citadel — the former seat of the Nguyen Dynasty (~200,000 VND entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike and explore the Royal Tombs south of the city — visit Tomb of Minh Mang or Tu Duc, set amid pine forests and lotus ponds (~100,000–150,000 VND each). Stop at Thien Mu Pagoda along the Perfume River.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Perfume River embankment at dusk. Explore Dong Ba Market for local souvenirs and snacks. Enjoy a traditional Hue dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Com Tam purchased near the train station on arrival — ~40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant — ~50,000–70,000 VND
meals.dinner: Hue royal cuisine set meal at a mid-range restaurant — try Banh Khoai (Hue crispy pancake) and Com Hen (baby clam rice) — ~100,000–150,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Hue can be hot and humid in April. Carry water and sunscreen. A bicycle rental is a great way to explore the tombs (~50,000–80,000 VND/day). Motorbike rental is faster (~150,000–200,000 VND/day).

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic bus or hire a car over the Hai Van Pass to Da Nang (~2.5 hours) — one of Vietnam's most spectacular coastal mountain roads. Stop at the summit for panoramic views of the sea and coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a hostel or guesthouse in Da Nang (~$15–$30/night). Visit the Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son) — a cluster of limestone hills with caves, pagodas, and city views (~40,000 VND). Explore the Buddhist sanctuaries inside the caves.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the iconic Dragon Bridge — if visiting on a weekend, stay until 9 PM to see the dragon breathe fire and water. Stroll along My Khe Beach at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Banh Canh or Chao (rice porridge) at a Hue street stall before departure — ~40,000 VND
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant near My Khe Beach — grilled fish, shrimp, and clams — ~120,000–180,000 VND
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (Da Nang-style turmeric noodles) at a local street restaurant — ~50,000–70,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Hai Van Pass is best enjoyed by motorbike for the full experience — consider renting one in Hue and dropping it off in Da Nang (easy rider tours available). Alternatively, book a seat on the Hue–Da Nang bus.

day_by_day.morning: Take a 30-minute bus or taxi to Hoi An Ancient Town (~30,000 VND by local bus). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Chinese Assembly Halls, and colorful merchant houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day Vietnamese cooking class in Hoi An (~$20–$30 USD) — visit the local market, learn to make Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings, then eat your creations. A perfect cultural and culinary experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Ancient Town after dark — the lantern-lit streets are magical at night. Buy a paper lantern (~20,000 VND) and release it on the Thu Bon River. Browse the night market for souvenirs and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — arguably Vietnam's most famous Banh Mi shop in Hoi An — ~30,000–50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Included in the cooking class
meals.dinner: White Rose dumplings and Cao Lau at a riverside restaurant in the Ancient Town — ~100,000–150,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An Ancient Town charges an entrance fee (~120,000 VND) which includes access to 5 heritage sites. Hoi An is very walkable and bicycle-friendly. Avoid peak afternoon hours as it can get crowded with tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bicycle ride through the rice paddies and villages surrounding Hoi An — head toward Tra Que Herb Village (~3 km from town) and join a short farming experience (~150,000 VND). A peaceful and authentic rural encounter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Da Nang by bus or taxi. Take a flight or sleeper bus to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — flight is ~1.5 hours (~$30–$60 USD on budget airlines like VietJet or Bamboo). Check into a hostel or guesthouse in District 1 or the Backpacker Street area (~$15–$30/night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bui Vien Walking Street — the heart of Saigon's backpacker scene. Grab a cold Saigon Beer, enjoy live music, and soak in the vibrant nightlife energy.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Xeo (sticky rice with mung bean and fried shallots) from a street cart in Hoi An — ~30,000 VND
meals.lunch: Quick Com Binh Dan (Vietnamese set rice meal) near Da Nang airport — ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa — one of Saigon's most legendary Banh Mi spots — ~50,000 VND, plus street snacks on Bui Vien

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City flight in advance for the best prices. Arrive at the airport at least 1.5 hours early. Grab a Grab (ride-hailing app) from the airport to your guesthouse — safer and cheaper than metered taxis.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering museum documenting the Vietnam War. Then walk to the nearby Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) — the former presidential palace with original 1970s decor intact.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day guided tour to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~$15–$20 USD including transport) — an extraordinary underground network used by Viet Cong fighters. Crawl through the tunnels and learn about guerrilla warfare history firsthand.
day_by_day.evening: Final night in Vietnam — head to the Ben Thanh Market area for last-minute souvenir shopping. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in District 1 with views of the city skyline. End the night with Vietnamese iced coffee and reflection on an incredible journey.

meals.breakfast: Pho at a classic Saigon pho shop near the hotel — ~60,000–80,000 VND
meals.lunch: Grilled snacks and fresh spring rolls (Goi Cuon) at a local spot near the Cu Chi Tunnels — ~80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range rooftop restaurant in District 1 — try Bo Luc Lac (shaking beef) or Banh Xeo (sizzling crepe) — ~150,000–250,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: The Cu Chi Tunnels tour typically departs at 8 AM and returns by 1–2 PM — book through your guesthouse or a reputable tour operator. If departing Vietnam tonight or tomorrow, allow time to pack and arrange airport transport. Tan Son Nhat Airport is ~30–45 min from District 1 by Grab.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.date: Day 1 – April 15, 2027 (Arrival Day)
day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter, Hanoi. Check-in, freshen up, and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll through the iconic 36 Streets of the Old Quarter – explore the narrow lanes, colonial architecture, and vibrant street life at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Guided evening walking tour of Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple (Jade Island Temple), beautifully lit at dusk. Soak in the atmosphere of the Old Quarter night market along Hang Dao Street.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel or a nearby premium café such as Kafé or The Note Coffee upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chả Cá Thăng Long – a legendary Hanoi restaurant famous for its signature turmeric-marinated grilled fish (chả cá), served tableside with dill, vermicelli, and roasted peanuts

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup in advance with a premium private car service. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. April in Hanoi is warm and humid (~28°C), so light breathable clothing is recommended.

day_by_day.date: Day 2 – April 16, 2027 (Hanoi Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Hoan Kiem Lake for a peaceful lakeside walk – witness locals practicing Tai Chi at sunrise. Visit the fully restored Ngoc Son Temple on the lake island. Followed by a guided cultural walk through the Old Quarter with a local expert historian, exploring the ancient guild streets and French colonial facades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology – one of Southeast Asia's finest museums, showcasing the 54 ethnic groups of Vietnam through immersive exhibits and outdoor reconstructed traditional homes. Private guided tour included. Afterward, explore the elegant French Quarter and the grand Hanoi Opera House (exterior and optional interior tour if available).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre – a uniquely Vietnamese art form dating back to the 11th century. Post-show, explore the vibrant Ta Hien Street (Beer Street) for an atmospheric evening in the Old Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Xôi Yến – a beloved local institution famous for premium sticky rice (xôi) dishes, a true Old Quarter institution
meals.lunch: Lunch at KOTO (Know One Teach One) – a social enterprise restaurant offering refined Vietnamese cuisine with a meaningful story
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane – a Michelin-recommended French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant set in a charming colonial villa, offering a refined tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book the Water Puppet Show in advance as it sells out quickly. The Museum of Ethnology is about 20 minutes from the Old Quarter – arrange a private car or premium taxi.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 – April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Heritage & Street Food Immersion)
day_by_day.morning: Private street food tour of the Old Quarter with a renowned local food guide. Sample iconic Hanoi breakfasts: Phở Bò (beef pho) at a legendary local stall, Bánh Mì from a premium bakery, and Bún Chả (grilled pork with rice noodles). Visit the historic Dong Xuan Market – Hanoi's largest covered market – for a sensory cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu) – Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070, a stunning example of traditional Vietnamese architecture. Followed by a visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (exterior and gardens), the Presidential Palace, and the iconic One Pillar Pagoda.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Sofitel Legend Metropole Hanoi – one of Asia's most iconic colonial hotels, offering panoramic views and world-class mixology. Dinner in the Old Quarter at your leisure.

meals.breakfast: Multi-stop street food breakfast as part of the guided tour – Phở Gia Truyền (a legendary pho stall on Bat Dan Street) is a must
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bún Chả Hương Liên – famously known as the restaurant where Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain dined together in 2016
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nhà Hàng Ngon (Restaurant Ngon) – a beautiful courtyard restaurant offering a curated menu of premium Vietnamese street food from all regions of the country

day_by_day.notes: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays. Verify opening hours in advance. Dress modestly for temple and mausoleum visits (covered shoulders and knees required).

day_by_day.date: Day 4 – April 18, 2027 (Halong Bay – Luxury Cruise Embarkation)
day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Hanoi Old Quarter to Halong Bay Marina (approximately 3.5 hours). Enjoy a premium en-route stop at a scenic viewpoint in the Halong region. Board your luxury overnight cruise vessel – premium options include Paradise Elegance, Indochine Cruise, or Scarlet Lady by Heritage Line.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise through the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Halong Bay, a breathtaking seascape of over 1,600 limestone karst islands. Guided kayaking or bamboo boat excursion through hidden lagoons and sea caves such as Luon Cave or Dark and Bright Cave. Onboard cooking demonstration – learn to prepare traditional Vietnamese spring rolls with the ship's chef.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the sundeck as the golden light illuminates the karst formations. Multi-course Vietnamese seafood dinner onboard, featuring freshly caught seafood and regional specialties paired with curated wines.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure or a premium grab-and-go arranged by the hotel
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch onboard the cruise ship – fresh Vietnamese cuisine with panoramic bay views
meals.dinner: Gourmet multi-course dinner onboard featuring fresh Halong Bay seafood – grilled squid, steamed clams, whole fish, and lobster (depending on the cruise package)

day_by_day.notes: Pack an overnight bag for the cruise. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and insect repellent. April weather in Halong Bay is generally pleasant (26–30°C) with low chance of rain. Confirm cruise booking at least 2 weeks in advance for luxury vessels.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 – April 19, 2027 (Halong Bay – Return to Hanoi / Fly to Hoi An)
day_by_day.morning: Early morning Tai Chi session on the sundeck at sunrise over the bay. Final kayaking or swimming excursion in a secluded cove. Brunch onboard before disembarking at the marina around 12:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer back to Hanoi (3.5 hours). Transfer to Noi Bai Airport for an afternoon domestic flight to Da Nang (approximately 1 hour 20 minutes). Arrival in Da Nang, then private car transfer to Hoi An Ancient Town (approximately 30 minutes). Check in to a luxury boutique hotel in or near Hoi An – recommended: Anantara Hoi An Resort, La Siesta Hoi An Resort & Spa, or Almanity Hoi An.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Hoi An – stroll through the magical lantern-lit Ancient Town (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Cross the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge and explore the atmospheric riverside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast onboard the cruise ship
meals.lunch: Brunch onboard before disembarkation
meals.dinner: Dinner at Morning Glory Restaurant in Hoi An – owned by celebrated chef Trinh Diem Vy, offering refined Central Vietnamese cuisine in an elegant colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights (Hanoi to Da Nang) well in advance. Vietnam Airlines or Bamboo Airways offer business class options. Coordinate airport transfers on both ends. Hoi An's Ancient Town is a short tuk-tuk or walking distance from most luxury hotels.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 – April 20, 2027 (Hoi An – Ancient Town & Cultural Immersion)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided walking tour of Hoi An Ancient Town – visit the Assembly Halls (Fujian, Cantonese), the 200-year-old Tan Ky Merchant House, and the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge. Learn about the town's multicultural trading history from the 15th–19th centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium hands-on Vietnamese cooking class at Red Bridge Cooking School or The Field Restaurant – set in a lush countryside farm setting. Learn to prepare Central Vietnamese specialties: Cao Lầu (Hoi An noodles), White Rose Dumplings (Bánh Bao Vạc), and Bánh Xèo (sizzling pancakes). Followed by a relaxing afternoon at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.evening: Release a traditional lantern on the Thu Bon River at sunset – a deeply symbolic and beautiful Hoi An tradition. Evening exploration of the lantern-lit Ancient Town, browsing silk tailors and artisan shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel – most luxury properties in Hoi An offer exceptional breakfast spreads with fresh local produce
meals.lunch: Lunch as part of the cooking class experience – enjoy what you've prepared in a beautiful riverside setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Field Restaurant – an immersive farm-to-table dining experience set among rice paddies, offering a curated menu of Central Vietnamese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Ancient Town is pedestrian-only in the evenings – wear comfortable shoes. The lantern release is best done just before dusk on the riverside. Tailor shops in Hoi An can create bespoke clothing within 24–48 hours – a premium souvenir worth considering.

day_by_day.date: Day 7 – April 21, 2027 (My Son Sanctuary & Countryside Exploration)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to My Son Sanctuary (UNESCO World Heritage Site) – a collection of ancient Cham Hindu temple ruins dating from the 4th–14th centuries, set in a lush jungle valley. A private guide provides in-depth historical and archaeological context. Depart early to beat the crowds and midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An via a scenic countryside route. Visit a local artisan village – Thanh Ha Pottery Village or Tra Que Vegetable Village – for an authentic rural cultural experience. Afternoon at leisure: optional bicycle ride through rice paddies and riverside villages, or relaxation at the hotel pool and spa.
day_by_day.evening: Premium cyclo (rickshaw) tour through the illuminated Ancient Town at dusk. Followed by a private rooftop dining experience or a premium riverside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure to My Son
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium local restaurant in the countryside near My Son, or a gourmet picnic arranged by the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mango Mango Restaurant – a chic, romantic riverside restaurant in the Ancient Town offering modern Vietnamese cuisine with beautiful river views

day_by_day.notes: My Son is approximately 40km from Hoi An (about 1 hour by private car). Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water and sunscreen. The site involves uneven terrain. Avoid visiting between 10:00–14:00 due to intense heat.

day_by_day.date: Day 8 – April 22, 2027 (Fly to Ho Chi Minh City – Saigon Arrival)
day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Hoi An – final stroll through the Ancient Town or relaxation at the hotel. Late morning checkout and private transfer to Da Nang Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Son Nhat Airport) – approximately 1 hour 20 minutes. Private luxury transfer to your accommodation in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City – recommended: Park Hyatt Saigon, The Reverie Saigon, or Capella Hanoi equivalent in Saigon. Check-in and freshen up. Afternoon exploration of the elegant Dong Khoi Street and the historic Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica of Saigon and the Central Post Office (designed by Gustave Eiffel).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Saigon Skydeck (Bitexco Financial Tower) or the EON Heli Bar for panoramic views of the city skyline. Followed by a premium dinner in District 1.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Hoi An hotel before checkout
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near Da Nang Airport, or a business class lounge meal if applicable
meals.dinner: Dinner at Noir – Dining in the Dark, Ho Chi Minh City – a unique, world-renowned dining concept where guests dine in complete darkness served by visually impaired staff, featuring a refined Vietnamese tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book Noir restaurant well in advance – it is one of HCMC's most popular premium dining experiences. Confirm hotel transfer from Tan Son Nhat Airport. Ho Chi Minh City traffic can be heavy in the afternoon – allow extra transfer time.

day_by_day.date: Day 9 – April 23, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City – History, Culture & Street Food)
day_by_day.morning: Private guided historical tour of Ho Chi Minh City: visit the Reunification Palace (Independence Palace) – a fascinating time capsule of the Vietnam War era; the War Remnants Museum – a powerful and moving exhibition on the Vietnam War; and the historic Ben Thanh Market for a curated premium street food experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Cholon (Chinatown) district – visit the ornate Thien Hau Pagoda and Binh Tay Market. Followed by a premium Vietnamese coffee culture experience at L'Usine or The Workshop – Saigon's finest specialty coffee establishments. Optional: visit to the Fine Arts Museum of Ho Chi Minh City for Vietnamese contemporary and classical art.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Saigon street food tour by motorbike (private xe om or tuk-tuk) through Districts 1, 3, and 4 – sampling Bánh Mì, Hủ Tiếu (Southern noodle soup), Bánh Xèo, and fresh tropical fruit. End the evening at a rooftop bar in District 1 for nightcaps with city views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel – the Park Hyatt Saigon and The Reverie offer exceptional breakfast experiences
meals.lunch: Premium street food lunch at Ben Thanh Market or Bến Thành Street Food Market – curated with a local guide to identify the finest stalls
meals.dinner: Street food progressive dinner as part of the evening motorbike tour, concluding with dessert at a premium patisserie such as Tous les Jours or Maison Marou (for premium Vietnamese craft chocolate)

day_by_day.notes: The War Remnants Museum is emotionally intense – allow sufficient time and emotional space. The motorbike street food tour is safe with a reputable operator; helmets are provided. Book through the hotel concierge for a vetted premium experience.

day_by_day.date: Day 10 – April 24, 2027 (Mekong Delta Day Trip & Farewell)
day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium private excursion to the Mekong Delta – depart early by private car to My Tho or Ben Tre (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Board a private wooden boat for a guided river cruise through the intricate network of canals and waterways. Visit a coconut candy workshop, a honey bee farm, and a tropical fruit orchard. Experience the unique floating market culture of the Delta.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ho Chi Minh City by private car. Afternoon at leisure for final shopping: visit premium Vietnamese craft and souvenir boutiques on Dong Khoi Street – Saigon Kitsch, Mekong Quilts, or Authentique Home for curated Vietnamese artisan goods. Final hotel relaxation, spa treatment, or pool time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premium restaurant of choice in District 1. Afterward, private luxury transfer to Tan Son Nhat Airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Mekong Delta lunch at a premium riverside restaurant in Ben Tre or My Tho – featuring fresh river fish, elephant ear fish (Cá Tai Tượng), and regional specialties
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Hoa Túc – a sophisticated Vietnamese restaurant set in a beautifully restored French colonial opium refinery, offering refined Southern Vietnamese cuisine in an atmospheric heritage setting

day_by_day.notes: The Mekong Delta tour should be booked through the hotel concierge with a premium private operator to ensure a personalized, crowd-free experience. Confirm departure flight time and arrange airport transfer accordingly. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Consider purchasing Vietnamese coffee, Phu Quoc pepper, and artisan lacquerware as premium gifts.
